subject: Endgame runbook & go/no-go triggers for pilot closure
messages:
From: Jordan Lewis <jordan.lewis@acmehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Endgame runbook & go/no-go triggers for pilot closure

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the prefix caching examples. We need to lock down what "success" looks like for our pilot so we can finalize internal approvals and budget cadence. At a high level we need a short, testable runbook that maps: key metrics, required smoke tests, ownership for each test, and explicit go/no-go triggers for the final demo to our board.

Two asks from my side:
- Can you draft a short MAP-style runbook with concrete pass/fail criteria for each test?
- Can you confirm that Redwood can provide the audit artifacts (token-level latency histograms, request logs) we requested for SOC2 evidence before the final demo?

We are targeting the week of 5/25 for the final internal demo and will need signoff from procurement + engineering by 5/28. Happy to take whatever format works best (spreadsheet or Google doc).

Appreciate it — Jordan

--
Jordan Lewis
Head of Infrastructure Programs | Acme Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lewis <jordan.lewis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Endgame runbook & go/no-go triggers for pilot closure

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a first-pass MAP runbook and attached it (MAP_v1.0.xlsx). High-level notes below and a proposed timeline.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Deliverable: MAP_v1.0.xlsx (tabbed: milestones, smoke tests, metrics, owners, rollback triggers)
- Core pass/fail signals: 95th latency <= 220ms for 90% of flows; end-to-end accuracy/concordance >= 92% on the provided test set; no PII leakage incidents in sampling; successful end-to-end test run (smoke) by each test owner.
- Ownership: Marissa will coordinate smoke tests and customer-facing acceptance; Ben will lead infrastructure readiness and audit artifact delivery; I will run the final cutover checklist and gating decision.

Proposed timeline:
- 5/20: Internal dry run of smoke tests (Redwood infra + Acme test harness)
- 5/22: Deliver audit artifacts (token-level latency histograms, request sampling, KV cache hit rates) — Ben owner
- 5/24: Joint smoke-test run with Acme test set, documented outcomes in MAP spreadsheet — Marissa owner
- 5/25–5/26: Buffer for fixes and re-run; final go/no-go recommendation by 5/27
- 5/28: Executive demo + formal signoff (Acme procurement + engineering)

A couple of clarifications: the "accuracy" target above is on the curated evaluation set you shared last month. If you want us to measure a different metric (e.g., F1 on entity extraction), tell us and we'll add it as a separate line item.

Attachments: MAP_v1.0.xlsx (spreadsheet), smoke-tests.md (test steps)

I copied Marissa and Ben to confirm owners and to add any infra-level constraints. If this structure looks right, we'll lock the MAP and start scheduling the runs.

Best,
Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lewis <jordan.lewis@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Endgame runbook & go/no-go triggers for pilot closure

Thanks Mina — the MAP looks good. I added a "test owners matrix" on the second tab and a short "acceptance test script" section to smoke-tests.md. Key additions:

- Test owners: Acme engineering (integration tests), Acme clinical (accuracy sampling), Redwood CS (user acceptance flows)
- Acceptance thresholds: concordance >= 92% (primary), false-positive rate <= 3% on flagged items (secondary), token-level cost per 1k requests within budget cap (Ben to confirm)
- Safety/rollback triggers: more than 2 critical mismatches in 3 consecutive sampling windows OR any observed PII leak => immediate rollback and investigation.

Ben — quick ask for you: can you confirm the artifact list we will hand off to Acme procurement for SOC2 evidence? I propose: token latency histogram (per-route), request sampling (anonymized), KV cache hit-rate summary, and audit log export for date range 5/01–5/25. If you can post a link to the artifacts in the shared Drive folder by 5/22 that will keep procurement moving.

Jordan — if you want, we can do a 30-minute runbook walkthrough tomorrow 5/21 at 9am PT to walk through owners and handoff points.

Cheers,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lewis <jordan.lewis@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Endgame runbook & go/no-go triggers for pilot closure

Marissa, Mina — this looks actionable, thanks. A few quick confirmations before the walkthrough tomorrow:

1) Audit artifacts: procurement will accept the anonymized request samples + latency histograms. We still need an HMAC for log exports — does Redwood provide a signed artifact or will we rely on our internal tooling to pull from a shared bucket?
2) Final demo: procurement wants a short acceptance checklist that they can sign off on (one page). Can you add a one-page "procurement acceptance checklist" tab to the spreadsheet?
3) Contingency: if we uncover a critical mismatch during the joint run on 5/24, is there an agreed SLA for remediation window (we'd like <= 48 hours for triage + initial fix)?

We'll join tomorrow's 9am PT walkthrough. I'll bring the procurement lead to confirm the checklist language.

Onward — Jordan
